items.title: As US funding cut for AU mission looms, Somalia faces reckoning it isn’t ready for
items.description: In 2023, Somalia’s government launched its most ambitious military campaign in years against Al-Shabab, a Somali armed group linked to Al-Qaeda. Somali troops and allied clan fighters pushed the group’s fighters out of large parts of central Somalia, and officials in Mogadishu, the capital, spoke confidently of finishing the group off within a year or two. By the spring of 2025, almost all of that ground was gone. Al-Shabab, moving carefully rather than charging back in, retook town after town during an offensive timed to the Muslim holy month of Ramadan, restoring a map of control that looked much like it had before the government’s push began. The reversal captures a dynamic that has defined this war for two decades. While Somali forces can clear territory of Al-Shabab, holding it is another matter — one heavily dependent on a multinational African Union peacekeeping force that now risks losing the funding that keeps it in the field. In early July, a leaked internal diplomatic note showed that the United States plans to block United Nations funding for the agency that supplies, caters for and moves the force around the country. Somali and regional officials, apparently caught off guard, have spent the weeks since scrambling for a way to keep the mission afloat. Somalia’s importance goes well beyond its own fight with Al-Shabab. The country hugs the coast of the Horn of Africa, along the southern edge of one of the world’s busiest shipping corridors, connecting the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean. General Dagvin Anderson, the top American general overseeing US military operations in Africa, has described Somalia as sitting on “ key terrain ” for exactly this reason, adding that the location alone “makes it important.” An Al-Shabab that controls Somalia’s coastline, as far as regional actors are concerned, threatens not just Somalia’s neighbours but potentially the security of those waterways. This is a large part of why so many outside powers have poured money and troops into propping up Somalia’s government over the past two decades, and why the funding crisis facing the African Union mission is not simply a Somali problem for them. … Washington has been remarkably direct about this calculation in the past, particularly when the stakes were high. In May 2009, as Somalia’s internationally-backed transitional government came close to being overrun by an earlier Al-Shabab attack, the US ambassador to Kenya sent a diplomatic cable to then-Secretary of State Hillary Clinton saying the government’s collapse would be “a major setback for US interests,” and that an Al-Shabab takeover, or a slide back into the lawlessness of Somalia’s earlier warlord years, would be treated as a threat to the US. Clinton immediately released emergency funds to the government and pushed the United Nations for a waiver to its arms embargo so more weapons could reach it. The US has its own concerns about the prospect of the Somali government collapsing and has been willing to take steps to prevent it. Part of that effort has involved an intense drone campaign targeting Al-Shabab and, more recently, Islamic State-Somalia. The US also has troops stationed in the country, including an expanded security presence along the Gulf of Aden and in Jubaland, along Somalia’s border with Kenya, where it operates a large base, a Somali defense official says. Other countries have also built significant relationships with Somalia’s federal government and its member states, giving them their own stakes in preventing an Al-Shabab takeover. While these interests vary, from security and military access to trade, infrastructure and regional influence, they mean that Somalia’s survival matters well beyond Washington. Turkey has built a deep military and economic footprint in Somalia, training Somali soldiers, operating the country’s main airport and port facilities, and now flying combat aircraft in support of Somali and African forces. It has also begun construction of a spaceport. Israel has recognized Somaliland and begun investing in ties with it, while the UAE has close commercial and security relationships with Puntland, Somaliland and Jubaland. Somalia’s security, in other words, is as much a contest over strategic territory and trade routes as it is a fight against a single insurgent group, even if fighting that group is the shared language every outside power can use in public. … Al-Shabab did not exist as a major force until an Ethiopian invasion in December 2006 transformed it into one. Before that, Mogadishu had briefly come under the control of the Islamic Courts Union (ICU), an alliance of clan elders, business figures and religious scholars that had restored a measure of order to the capital after fifteen years of rule by rival warlords. Al-Shabab had already splintered from the ICU months earlier as a harder-line faction with narrower religious goals, but it was still a minor player. Ethiopia’s decision to invade had little to do with Al-Shabab specifically. Addis Ababa viewed the ICU’s rise negatively, wary of both its religious leanings and its ambitions toward the Somali-inhabited Ogaden region, which Somalia had invaded back in 1977. Ethiopia’s then prime minister, Meles Zenawi, framed the operation publicly as a defensive response to attacks staged from Somali territory. Washington backed the operation and worked closely with Addis Ababa to plan it. American special forces entered Somalia alongside Ethiopian troops, and the US supplied intelligence, satellite imagery and logistical support. The invasion that followed married two separate motives. Ethiopia’s fear of a hostile government on its border, and America’s post-September 11 worries about Somalia becoming a new safe haven for Al-Qaeda. Ethiopian troops ousted the ICU from Mogadishu within weeks, but their continued presence in the city proved deeply unpopular and fed the very insurgency they had aimed to prevent. A UN-backed African Union peacekeeping force deployed alongside them from March 2007 to protect Somalia’s internationally recognized, but weak, transitional government. Al-Shabab emerged in that maelstrom as a religious-nationalist movement resisting the occupation of Somalia by forces from neighbouring countries. It merged with Al-Qaeda in 2012. Ethiopia, exhausted by an occupation it had not planned to sustain, withdrew in January 2009, leaving the African force to prop up the Somali state largely on its own. That African force, first known as AMISOM, evolved from a defensive deployment into an active combat mission that helped Somali troops push Al-Shabab out of Mogadishu and other major cities. Over time, it became the African Union’s deadliest, largest and most expensive peacekeeping operation, with troop numbers in the mid-2010s exceeding 20,000 covering an area in south central Somalia roughly the size of Iraq. It was succeeded in 2022 by a transitional mission called ATMIS, and then, at the start of 2025, by the current mission, the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), which is meant to be the final stage of a gradual handover of security responsibility to Somali forces in 2029. … Despite this timetable, however, the Somali defense official tells Mada Masr that the country’s forces are not yet ready to take full responsibility for security. The source says the Somali army is mainly a light infantry force that is relatively capable of offensive operations to push Al-Shabab out of towns and cities, but struggles to hold them when Al-Shabab attacks. The same source says the African Union’s peacekeepers were more heavily armed and better equipped to play that role in the broader fight against Al-Shabab. The most striking example came with the dramatic reversal of a major clan-led, government-backed offensive launched by President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud in 2023, which Al-Shabab almost completely rolled back during its 2025 Ramadan offensive. Though Somali defense officials have bristled at the description of the situation between Al-Shabab and the Somali army as a “ stalemate ” in a recent International Crisis Group report, arguing that the Somali army is significantly more powerful, that strength has not translated into major territorial gains or the recapture of many towns from the group. General Dagvin Anderson, the AFRICOM commander, recently complained after a meeting with Somali officials that he was still discussing how to liberate territory that Somali forces had previously cleared when he was serving in a more junior role in special forces operations. “This is what causes the frustration,” he said , “because that territory was lost because somewhere the focus on terrorism was not there and was elsewhere.” After years of fighting, the battlelines haven’t changed much. The capital’s hinterlands remain vulnerable to Al-Shabab attacks, even in areas where the group does not have direct control. Further north, Al-Shabab controls a vast swathe of territory stretching from Middle Juba in Jubaland to Galgaduud. Government control is largely confined to pockets of territory with vast stretches beyond its reach. And for now, the government is projecting an image of control, especially in urban areas under its control. Ethiopian troops have begun preparing for a planned handover of a forward operating base in Burhakaba, one of their deepest positions in Somalia. There has also been a sustained decrease in violence and fatalities in the capital. And the government has killed scores of Al-Shabab’s senior leaders, Somalia’s intelligence agency said earlier this year. A former Somali intelligence source attributed the decline partly to the government’s increased capacity to monitor and confront the group and partly to a shift in Al-Shabab’s strategy away from mass-casualty attacks on Mogadishu. The city is more fortified than before, and the Somali intelligence and a Somali security source, as well as Western diplomats interviewed, say its fall was not something they were immediately concerned about. Elsewhere in Somalia, Al-Shabab has maintained a higher tempo of attacks, particularly in the Lower Shabelle region, which saw an almost 60% increase in attacks between June and August compared with earlier this year. Attacks have also increased in northern Kenya, where five members of Kenya’s security forces were killed in July. The African Union’s forces operate in sectors distributed among the country’s troop-contributing forces to contain Al-Shabab and hold territory. Kenya has a large presence in the border region with Jubaland, as does Ethiopia, whose troops cross into the neighbouring South West State. Ugandan troops, among the first to take part in the mission, are heavily concentrated around the capital, while contingents of Burundian and Djiboutian troops are positioned northeast of them, along the road to Beledweyne and then into Galmudug. These deployments are spread across 49 locations. Excluding troops stationed in Somalia under bilateral arrangements, the force is believed to number just under 12,000. Many of these soldiers spend long periods of time deployed to relatively remote regions of Somalia, in extremely dangerous circumstances. According to one account by a former Djiboutian peacekeeper in the Africa Defense Forum journal, published by AFRICOM, his unit endured a 24-month deployment marked by “repeated exposure to stressful and traumatic events,” after which morale declined and some troops “began to mentally check out, losing focus.” For those forces, the United Nations Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS), the agency the US is cutting funds for, is a critical backbone of their operations. It provides fuel, water and food rations; casualty and medical evacuation; air transport; and the communications, engineering and equipment support that let troops deploy, move and stay in the field. A Western security analyst focused on Somalia tells Mada Masr that these forces operating, especially in the southern regions, won’t be able to remain safely in the field without the backing of UNSOS or some alternative. “Al-Shabab would find it easy to attack and exhaust those particularly exposed bases, and they would be sitting ducks without UNSOS,” the source says. “If no credible replacement is agreed before December, the risk is not simply a smaller mission. It is an irreversibly degraded mission,” the Somali research group Balqiis Insights stated in a report published last month. Mohamud Madowe Abdullahi, a field researcher based in Jubaland with extensive experience coordinating humanitarian access in hard-to-reach regions, tells Mada Masr that cutting off funding to UNSOS would be like “giving the land to Al-Shabab.” He adds that AU forces also support nearby communities, distributing food and bringing doctors to remote areas. “There is a lot more happening than just holding ground against Al-Shabab,” Abdullahi says. The African Union’s peacekeeping missions in Somalia have historically faced major funding challenges, which they have usually been able to muddle through, a Western diplomatic source tells Mada Masr. Previous financing events for AUSSOM have seen some countries step up with partial pledges, though never enough to close the gap, despite hopes among Somali and Western officials that countries might step in to bridge the shortfall. At a recent such event, held in New York on September 25 last year, the AU pledged US$20 million toward AUSSOM’s estimated $196-million 2025 budget, and the United Kingdom pledged 16.5 million British pounds, with several other countries committing to support. In April the European Union committed 75 million euros to AUSSOM. A UN secretary-general’s report published in May put AUSSOM’s funding gap at $38.5 million, against a total budget of $154.7 million. UNSOS, the mission’s logistics arm, was dealing with its own shortfall of $130 million. That came after Washington withheld its share of UNSOS funding, roughly a quarter of the budget, in August 2025. A second Western diplomatic source says the mission, in its current form, was “unaffordable,” given the persistent difficulty of securing the funding needed to sustain it, and that a slimmed-down version might have to be accepted. Resolution 2719, passed by the UN Security Council (UNSC), would let AUSSOM draw up to 75 percent of its funding from UN assessed contributions, but the US has consistently opposed using it for this mission. It blocked the move in May 2025, after issuing a warning in late 2024, and left it out again in December 2025 when the UNSC renewed AUSSOM’s mandate under Resolution 2809. During the December 2025 meeting, Jeff Bartos, the US ambassador to the UN, delivered a blistering criticism of Somalia’s performance against Al-Shabab. He complained that significant funds had been poured into the mission, but that the returns so far had been limited and that it wouldn’t be the US’s problem to sustain it. “Despite the sacrifices of the troops and police and the long-term support from the United States and other partners and allies, sustained progress against the terrorism threat in the region and towards the essential transfer of most security functions to Somalia has been elusive,” Bartos told the council . Bartos added that the responsibility for combatting Al-Shabab should be shifted “primarily” to those who have the most at stake. Samira Gaid, a regional security expert at the Balqiis Insights think tank, tells Mada Masr that the US had warned the government in 2024 about an impending decision to cut funding for UNSOS, but that the government had “buried its head in the sand instead of developing a strategy to manage it.” Gaid expects that, absent a fix for UNSOS, Somalia will need a series of bilateral agreements with individual troop-contributing countries, funded from other sources, to keep foreign forces in the country. For Afyare Elmi, a Somali academic, there are one of two scenarios that could now play out in Somalia in light of the US decision. “There could be a rupture,” he tells Mada Masr, warning that the mission could collapse and Al-Shabab could recapture urban areas across south-central Somalia. Alternatively, he says, a political solution could be found that delays the funding cut and allows the mission to continue while a more sustainable solution is developed. “Either way, things need to change,” he says. A senior Somali official plays down the idea that the US decision reflects a specific rift with Somalia and was part of a broader American shift away from multilateralism and UN-led initiatives. Instead, the official says Washington is pursuing a more targeted policy, seeking leverage points where US interests and capabilities can produce tangible results, including through deeper engagement with Somalia’s autonomous regional governments. … Somali officials have said that they still consider the US a “ strategic ” counter-terrorism partner. A former senior defense official tells Mada Masr that the relationship is underpinned by “one common enemy”, Al-Shabab, adding that this “won’t change unless the US’s view of Al-Shabab changes.” US President Donald Trump’s current administration has increased its air, drone and ground operations against Al-Shabab, with the number already surpassing Trump’s previous record for a single presidency. It has also partnered with Puntland forces in their offensive against IS-Somalia and with Jubaland’s forces against Al-Shabab. In recent weeks, too, an AFRICOM delegation visited Somalia, travelling to the federal capital, Puntland and Jubaland. During his visit, General Dagvin Anderson, the AFRICOM commander, attempted to allay fears of US re-trenchment from Somalia, explaining that the two countries have a mutual interest in cooperating against Al-Shabab. Somalia, he added, “sits on key terrain”, and so “that alone makes it important.” He ruled out US recognition of Somaliland, a breakaway territory in the north, a major concern for Somali officials. But crucially, he appeared to condition future US engagement in Somalia on an end to what he called “political infighting,” a reference to the government’s frequent use of federal resources to pursue and battle political opponents rather than Al-Shabab. During the latter part of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s term, the government’s fight against its political opponents has only intensified. After Jubaland President Ahmed Madobe was re-elected in an uncompetitive election in November 2024, the federal government sent forces into the state. They were defeated by Jubaland’s forces. In Baidoa, the federal government forcibly removed Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed, known as Laftagareen, after he attempted to do the same earlier this year. In recent weeks, the federal government has also sent forces to Puntland, prompting Puntland to seize three military bases belonging to federal forces in the state. Both Jubaland and Puntland have severed ties with the central government. A more controversial move came when Somalia’s parliament amended the constitution months before the president’s term was due to end, extending it by a year. The government’s mandate was due to expire in May. It also sought to introduce a one-person, one-vote election system, a move fiercely opposed by two federal states and the Mogadishu-based opposition, who don’t believe such a contest would be competitive. Somalia’s political and security issues overlapped when the Somali Future Council (SFC) — an opposition umbrella including a former president, former prime ministers, and the sitting presidents of Puntland and Jubaland — wrote to participating countries before the second extraordinary summit of AUSSOM troop-contributing countries, which took place in Uganda in July, arguing that the funding crisis itself was a symptom of Somalia’s political dysfunction, and urging them to make a Somali-led political settlement, including a transitional council to oversee the country’s stalled constitutional and electoral transition, a condition of their continued support. It was dismissed by the government and its backers as an attempt to return Somalia to transitional governance. Somalia’s president strongly resisted attempts to mention the country’s internal political disputes in the final communiqué from Kampala. The issues had initially been mentioned without controversy in the days leading up to the July 31 heads-of-state meeting, a third Somali official says. But Mohamud was apparently unhappy when he saw them included in the final text he received. “Local politics of Somalia must not be internationalized, regionalized,” he said at the summit, adding that because the communiqué was going to the UN and AU, Somalia didn’t want that. That resistance to outside scrutiny drew a pointed rebuke from Mohamed Abdi Ware, a veteran figure in Somalia’s political class who now serves as deputy executive secretary of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), an East African regional body. After the meeting, he was accused allegedly by government officials of “backstabbing” Somalia for allowing its internal affairs to be raised at the regional forum. Ware blasted the government, pointing to the moral hazard: “the irony of asking for foreign troops to maintain basic security in one’s own country and yet claim ‘sovereignty’ when convenient was not lost on the delegates of the Summit.” Ware warned that avoiding a “precipitous”, “premature” and “disorderly” exit for the peacekeepers was necessary to avoid giving Al-Shabab an “enormous strategic advantage now, and for a long time.” Though Uganda’s president, Yoweri Museveni, has committed his troops to remaining in Somalia regardless of what happens with UNSOS, one of the key takeaways from the meetings was the summit’s call to extend UNSOS’s funding for 18 to 24 months, to allow for an orderly, phased exit. Another Western diplomatic source echoes this, saying they wanted the US not to pull out so abruptly. countries have also reportedly been approached about possibly plugging the financing gap for UNSOS, according to the third Somali official. … The US’s broader position on Somalia has also come into focus after a series of high-level engagements with the country’s autonomous states. US generals have met leaders in Puntland and Jubaland , while a Somaliland delegation visited AFRICOM headquarters in Stuttgart, Germany. The US has also agreed with Puntland to expand a military facility about 25 km west of Bosaso, the region’s strategic coastal commercial hub. AFRICOM has stated the site is not a military base. A Puntland official tells Mada Masr that the facility was used to support its campaign against IS-Somalia, while the US was deepening its presence to better manage maritime threats in the Gulf of Aden and conduct counterterrorism operations. Washington has also committed to enhancing cooperation with Jubaland, a frontline state in Somalia’s fight against Al-Shabab. In late July, a delegation of 11 US lawmakers visited Kismayo, Jubaland’s capital. The delegation was led by Republican Representative Ronny Jackson. The Somali defense official and the two Western officials say the visits to Somalia’s regions do not signal an official revival of the US’s previous dual-track strategy, under which Washington engaged separately with the country’s autonomous regions and federal government. The second Western diplomatic official says the US is too invested in Somalia’s federal government to simply pivot north and disengage from Mogadishu. The senior Somali defense official says all US engagement was still taking place through the federal government, but acknowledges that Washington was concerned about security in the Gulf of Aden and along the Kenyan border, where the US operates a large military base at Manda Bay that was attacked in 2020. Last year, the US offered a $10-million reward for information leading to the capture of one of the attackers and his poster has been plastered across Kismayo. “They have those interests here and so fair enough, it also helps us too,” the official tells Mada Masr. The Somali defense official tells Mada Masr that Washington now views Somalia through a narrower lens, focused primarily on securing its own interests in migration, counterterrorism and maritime security and containing security threats emerging from the country. In July, the US asked Somalia to extradite two suspects in a fraud and homicide case which it complied with. The second senior Somali official tells Mada Masr that Somalia’s decision to accept the request was an attempt to curry favour with Washington. The US has long been one of Somalia’s key security partners and, until recently, its main humanitarian partner. That changed after the US government cut its global aid programmes. The Trump administration has also complicated US-Somali relations through the president’s frequent disparaging remarks about the country, as well as a broader perception that some officials in his Republican Party view Somaliland, the breakaway northern region, as a better partner. Somali officials have sought to steer clear of the comments. In December, Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre said , “sometimes there are things you simply let pass.” That strategy, however, won’t resolve Somalia’s broader conundrum. All Somali officials, western diplomats and western security officials who spoke to Mada Masr say they did not believe the international community was prepared to allow Somalia to be overrun as Kabul was in 2021. Most also said they did not believe Al-Shabab could realistically achieve that at present. Nevertheless, the clock is still ticking. “Doomsday is not really on the horizon immediately,” says the second Western diplomatic source, “but we could be there in around a year or two if we don’t stem the tide now.” The post As US funding cut for AU mission looms, Somalia faces reckoning it isn’t ready for first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Gov’t is reviewing tax laws to keep pace with changing economy – Vice President
items.description: Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang says the government is undertaking a comprehensive review of Ghana’s tax laws to simplify compliance, improve fairness, and ensure the country’s tax regime keeps pace with a rapidly changing economy. According to her, the review forms part of broader efforts to modernise Ghana’s tax administration through the adoption of technology, improved data systems, and stronger engagement with taxpayers. She made the remarks at the Ghana Revenue Authority’s annual Tax Conference in Accra on Wednesday, August 19. “We are undertaking a broader review of Ghana’s core tax legislation to simplify compliance, improve equity and competitiveness, and ensure that our tax laws keep pace with the changing economy,” she said. The Vice President said tax reform extends beyond introducing new policies and requires efficient administration and stronger partnerships between the state and taxpayers. She said the government was continuing to digitise tax administration to improve efficiency and strengthen revenue mobilisation. “Our VAT reforms are being supported by measures, including improved systems for taxing cross-border transactions on digital platforms and the introduction of fiscal electronic devices to strengthen compliance and monitoring,” she said. She stressed that the government and the Ghana Revenue Authority could not achieve the country’s tax reform objectives alone, highlighting the critical role tax professionals play in strengthening the tax system. The Vice President said tax practitioners serve as a bridge between the state and taxpayers by interpreting legislation, advising individuals and businesses, helping taxpayers meet their obligations, and contributing to the development of tax policy. She urged tax professionals to continue providing the expertise needed to build a more effective, equitable, and responsive tax system capable of supporting Ghana’s long-term economic development.

items.title: Syrian FM Shaibani due to visit Pakistan today: FO
items.description: Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani is due to visit Pakistan at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement on Wednesday. The visit comes as Syria’s transitional leadership pursues regional and international engagement following the overthrow of Bashar al-Assad in 2024. According to the statement, Shaibani would undertake the visit from August 19-20 and will be accompanied by a high-level delegation. “During the visit, the two sides will hold in-depth discussions across the entire spectrum of bilateral relations, review avenues for further enhancing bilateral cooperation, and exchange views on regional and international developments,” the statement read. The FO noted that the visit marks an important step towards further enhancing bilateral relations and cooperation between Pakistan and Syria. The visit will be the first by a Syrian foreign minister since Walid al-Mouallem travelled to Pakistan in May 2007 and the first since the change of government in Damascus. Earlier today, the FO strongly condemned an “unprovoked” attack carried out by Israel on an airbase in Syria, saying such acts had the potential to “further undermine regional peace and stability”. Syria’s state-run Ekhbariya television, citing a military source, said on Tuesday that Israel carried out eight airstrikes on the runway and storage facilities at the Abu al-Duhur base near Aleppo in northwest Syria. A separate military source and a civilian who lived near the base said there were no casualties. “Such provocative actions constitute a flagrant violation of international law and have the potential to further undermine regional peace and stability,” the FO said on Wednesday. “Pakistan expresses its unwavering solidarity with the brotherly people of Syria, and reiterates its full support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity as well as peace and prosperity of the Syrian Arab Republic.”

items.title: Accident sur le pont de Sakoinsé : Du cyanure de sodium détecté dans les eaux du Nazinon
items.description: Suite à l'accident de la circulation au niveau du pont de Sakoinsé survenu dans la nuit du 14 au 15 août 2026, les autorités burkinabè suivent de près la situation environnementale du fleuve. Dans un communiqué en date du 19 août 2026, le ministre d'État, ministre de l'Agriculture, de l'Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le Commandant Ismaël Sombié, indique que les opérations d'urgence ont permis de récupérer la totalité du produit encore présent dans le fleuve après l'accident. Des prélèvements d'eau ont également été réalisés par les laboratoires spécialisés dans l'analyse de la qualité de l'eau et de l'environnement pour évaluer l'ampleur de la contamination et suivre son évolution. Les premières analyses ont confirmé la présence de cyanure de sodium dans les eaux du Nazinon. Face à cette situation, le gouvernement assure que les mesures prises ont permis de stabiliser la pollution. Toutefois, un suivi environnemental et sanitaire rigoureux se poursuit afin de garantir l'élimination complète des effets de la contamination et le retour progressif à une situation normale. En attendant les résultats complets des analyses en cours, les populations riveraines sont invitées à observer strictement les mesures de précaution édictées par les services compétents. Il leur est notamment demandé de ne pas utiliser ni consommer l'eau du fleuve et de s'abstenir de consommer les poissons ou autres animaux retrouvés morts dans la zone affectée jusqu'à nouvel ordre. Les autorités précisent que des analyses sont effectuées quotidiennement et que toute information susceptible de contribuer à la protection des populations sera communiquée au fur et à mesure de l'évolution de la situation. Le ministre d'État a également rappelé aux importateurs, distributeurs et utilisateurs de produits chimiques leur responsabilité dans le respect des normes environnementales relatives au transport, au stockage et à la distribution de ces substances. À cet effet, des contrôles seront renforcés par les services de la police environnementale. Lefaso.net

items.title: Don de sang : plus de 100 poches collectées en une journée à Ziguinchor
items.description: Plus de 100 poches de sang ont été collectées, mercredi, au Centre départemental d’éducation populaire et sportive (CDEPS) de Ziguinchor, à l’occasion d’une journée de don de sang organisée par le Service départemental de la Jeunesse et des Sports. Présidée par l’adjoint au préfet de Ziguinchor, Modou Samb, l’activité a enregistré une forte mobilisation de la jeunesse, des mouvements sportifs, des forces de défense et de sécurité, ainsi que de plusieurs services de l’État. « Nous avons voulu placer la jeunesse, les mouvements sportifs et les forces de défense et de sécurité au cœur d’un acte citoyen capable de sauver des vies. Les forces de défense et de sécurité ont répondu massivement à l’appel, démontrant ainsi, une fois encore, que le concept armée-nation n’est pas un simple slogan, mais une réalité », a déclaré Seydina Ka, chef du Service départemental de la Jeunesse et des Sports et directeur du CDEPS de Ziguinchor. Selon lui, la collecte a largement dépassé les prévisions des organisateurs. « Nous avons été agréablement surpris par l’ampleur de la mobilisation. Nous pensions difficilement atteindre un tel niveau de collecte. Mais nous avons finalement largement dépassé la barre des 100 poches. C’est une très bonne nouvelle pour les structures sanitaires de la région », s’est-il félicité. Des agents de la Sonaged et plusieurs autres services de l’État ont également pris part à cette campagne de don de sang. Cette initiative intervient dans un contexte marqué par un déficit de poches de sang dans plusieurs établissements sanitaires de la région. « Il y a quelques semaines, nous avions été informés d’un déficit important de poches de sang dans les établissements sanitaires. La situation est suffisamment préoccupante pour que chacun se sente concerné. Le don de sang constitue aujourd’hui une urgence absolue et nous devons unir nos forces pour contribuer à combler ce déficit », a souligné Seydina Ka. La collecte de plus de 100 poches devrait ainsi contribuer au renforcement des stocks disponibles dans les structures sanitaires de la région. Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)

items.title: Two remanded over alleged theft of GH¢932,040 fuel, tanker fire
items.description: An Accra Circuit Court has remanded two persons accused of stealing 54,000 litres of petrol valued at GH¢932,040 and subsequently setting fire to the tanker transporting the fuel. Alhassan Amidu, a driver, and Francis Owusu, a driver’s mate, are alleged to have conspired to steal the fuel and burn the tanker, valued at GH¢980,000, in an attempt to make the incident appear to be an accident. The two have been charged with conspiracy to commit crime, namely stealing and causing damage, as well as stealing and causing damage. They have pleaded not guilty to the charges. The prosecution told the court that the complainant, Emmanuel Narh, owns J.K. Narh Transport, a fuel transportation company. According to the prosecution, Amidu was the driver of the tanker, with registration number BRU JK 9171-21, while Owusu was the driver’s mate. The court heard that the accused persons were assigned to transport the 54,000 litres of petrol from Tema to Buipe in the Savannah Region. The prosecution alleged that the two conspired to sell the fuel before setting fire to the tanker on a stretch of road between Kawakpe and Gurupe while travelling towards Buipe. The accused persons subsequently informed the complainant that the tanker and its contents had been destroyed by fire in an accident, the prosecution said. The complainant, however, suspected foul play and reported the matter to the police, leading to the arrest of the two accused persons. During investigations, the prosecution said the accused persons admitted in their caution statements that they had tampered with the tanker’s compartment seal by drilling into it to gain access to the fuel. Investigations are continuing. The two accused persons are expected to reappear before the court on August 31, 2026.

items.title: NPP lacks credibility to make impact in 2028 election – Mustapha Gbande
items.description: The Deputy General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Mustapha Gbande, has stated that the New Patriotic Party (NPP) lacks credibility to make any impact in the 2028 general election. “Will the NPP accept responsibility for the misuse and mismanagement of state resources while they were in government for eight years?” he asked. Speaking in an interview about the successful conduct of the NPP’s regional executive elections, Mr Gbande said changing executives was a routine exercise for all political parties. Culture He said what the NPP did was not a new culture, stressing that the new executives were all old members of the party who contributed to the mess the country had found itself in. He said the credibility of the party was critical to its success. While commending the NPP for the peaceful conduct of the regional elections, Mr Gbande said they might have all the ideas but if they lacked credibility the party could never be successful. He alleged that the flag bearer of the NPP, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, supported a number of candidates but those candidates lost. He said the NPP election did not show the bottom up approach of reorganisation. Mr Gbande said the NPP missed the moments and benefits of sober reflection after the humiliating defeat before reorganising, stressing that “they rather thought being evasive towards government will bring them together faster but that is also failing.” New era Mr Gbande said the country had moved to a new era of politics where the citizenry abhorred mismanagement, corruption and misuse of state resources. He said the NDC government under the leadership of President John Dramani Mahama was cleaning the mess the NPP left behind while in government. Mr Gbande said while Ghanaians appreciated the lean government being operated by President Mahama, the NPP was very uncomfortable. Background The NPP successfully conducted its regional executive elections, with the outcome seen as more than an internal housekeeping exercise. The post-2024 data shows a party that lost ground far beyond its traditional swing zones. The collapse was steepest in the Greater Accra Region, from 21 parliamentary seats in 2016 to just five in 2024. In the Ashanti Region, which is the “heartbeat” of the party, the NPP lost eight of its 47 seats in that stronghold. More worrying for strategists, the NDC’s vote share climbed from a ceiling of 28 per cent to 35 per cent. Belief The NPP acknowledges that what unites them is the brief to rebuild trust with members, re-engage floating voters, and deliver parliamentary seats. The party knows that its 2024 loss was not just organisational but was about voter perception of the economy, jobs and cost of living.

items.title: Prudential Bank equips young professionals with practical personal finance skills at National Youth Mentorship Summit
items.description: The Head of Distribution and Channels at Prudential Bank LTD, Kojo Nteh, has encouraged young professionals to develop disciplined financial habits and make informed money decisions as the foundation for long-term financial security and wealth creation. Speaking at the National Youth Mentorship Summit held in Accra, Mr. Nteh called on young professionals to adopt disciplined financial habits early in their careers, warning that without a plan, money will find its own plan to leave. Addressing the audience on the theme “Personal Finance Tips for the Young Professional,” he noted that while earning an income is important, financial success ultimately depends on how effectively individuals manage their finances. He introduced the concept of “paying yourself first”; setting aside a portion of your income for savings before spending on anything else. “It doesn’t matter how much you save,” he said. “What matters is consistency. Before you pay everyone else, make sure you pay yourself. The same way you would pay for transport, food and clothes. That is what you will use in the future,” He urged participants to develop spending plans before receiving their income, stressing that budgeting helps individuals align their spending with their financial goals while avoiding unnecessary expenses. He further advised the young professionals to automate their savings through standing orders, saying that removing the temptation to spend first makes it easier to build healthy financial habits. “If on the day you are paid, the deduction goes through automatically, after some time you will get used to using whatever is left. You will adjust and manage on what remains,” he explained. Mr. Nteh also cautioned against get-rich-quick schemes and speculative investments that promise unrealistic returns, urging the youth to exercise patience and make informed financial decisions. Additionally, he encouraged participants to resist lifestyle inflation by increasing their savings as their incomes grow rather than matching every salary increment with higher spending. Mr. Nteh left the young professionals with a charge, “Be consistent. Be patient. Start small but start now. The habits you build today will determine the wealth you have tomorrow.” The National Youth Mentorship Summit brought together students, graduates and young professionals to engage with industry leaders on career development, leadership and financial empowerment.

items.title: ‘They found the wrong target’ – Sammy Gyamfi hits back at Afenyo-Markin
items.description: Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, has accused Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin of using what he describes as a sustained campaign of allegations against the institution to exert pressure on its management. His latest comments come amid a growing dispute over GoldBod’s financial performance, with Mr Afenyo-Markin alleging that the institution has incurred a GH¢22 billion loss. The Effutu MP has also warned that current GoldBod officials could face stringent bail conditions in the future if the New Patriotic Party (NPP) returns to power. Mr Gyamfi has strongly rejected the claims, describing them as false and pointing to GoldBod’s audited 2025 financial statements. According to him, the institution recorded an operational surplus of GH¢907 million and an overall surplus of GH¢5.4 billion for the year ended December 31, 2025. He has also defended GoldBod’s performance in the local gold value chain, particularly its efforts to increase refining and value addition. “These are devious extortionists and political mercenaries who will come at you with lies to tarnish your reputation in the hope that you will fold and settle for what they call ‘compulsory arbitration’ and through that, oil their palms,” Mr Gyamfi said. He insisted that he would not be intimidated by the allegations or threats arising from the political dispute over GoldBod. “Well, this time around, they found the wrong target,” he added, as the exchange between the GoldBod CEO and the Minority Leader continues to intensify.

items.title: Euthanasie : Macron promulgue une loi qui laisse planer le spectre des dérives
items.description: La promulgation par le president de la Republique de la loi instaurant un « droit a l'aide a mourir » marque l'aboutissement d'un parcours parlementaire long et heurte. Publie ce mercredi 19 août au Journal officiel, le texte, vote au milieu du mois de juillet , ouvre la voie, sous conditions, a l'administration d'un produit letal pour certains patients. Pourtant, loin de clore les debats, cette decision reveille des inquietudes persistantes sur la protection des plus fragiles et la solidite des garde-fous annonces. Des recours limites et un dialogue juge incomplet Pour y acceder, le patient doit etre majeur, de nationalite francaise ou resident de longue date, souffrir d'une affection « grave et incurable » en phase terminale ou avancee, endurer des douleurs physiques insupportables et conserver jusqu'au bout une volonte libre et eclairee. Un medecin tranche, apres consultation d'autres professionnels. En cas d'incapacite physique, un soignant peut administrer le produit letal. Mais les decrets d'application restent a publier, reportant l'entree en vigueur effective. Le Conseil constitutionnel a valide le dispositif avec quelques reserves. Emmanuel Macron a salue un « debat democratique exemplaire ». Fin de vie: Emmanuel Macron a promulgué la loi. pic.twitter.com/J5TtA9bgeg — Thierry de Cabarrus (@tcabarrus) August 19, 2026 Pourtant, le Senat s'y est oppose a plusieurs reprises, et cinq saisines, dont une inhabituelle du Premier ministre, ont illustre les fractures. Les recours des proches ou tiers restent tres limites avant l'acte, concentres sur le juge administratif et, surtout, accessibles au patient lui-meme. La Fondation Jerome Lejeune s'est dit « indignee », tandis que l'association Les eligibles et leurs Aidants denonce « le danger total de cette loi pour les plus vulnerables ». Ces alertes ne sont pas isolees. Sur X, des voix deplorent cette promulgation, a l'image de l'avocat Erwan Le Morhedec, chroniqueur pour le journal La Croix , deplore : « Promulgation de la loi "aide a mourir". Normal. Emmanuel Macron aura probablement sa premiere euthanasie avant la fin de son mandat. De quoi parachever l'ambiance crepusculaire ordinaire d'une fin de regne ». Promulgation de la loi "aide à mourir". Normal. Emmannuel Macron aura probablement sa première euthanasie avant la fin de son mandat. De quoi parachever l'ambiance crépusculaire ordinaire d'une fin de règne. — Erwan Le Morhedec (@koztoujours) August 19, 2026 D'autres rappellent l'experience neerlandaise, ou les criteres se sont progressivement elargis au-dela des intentions initiales, suscitant des derives documentees avec notamment l'execution d'un patient de 12 ans . La presidente de la Confederation nationale des Associations familiales catholiques, Pascale Moriniere, appelle a la mobilisation pour l'election presidentielle : « Prochaine etape : enjoindre les candidats a l'election presidentielle d'abroger cette loi euthanasie et suicide assiste ». Prochaine étape : enjoindre les candidats a l'élection présidentielle d'abroger cette loi #euthanasie et #suicideassisté https://t.co/fqusJInBvn — Pascale Morinière (@pascalemorinie1) August 19, 2026 En France, le manque de dialogue reel avec une partie des soignants et des associations, et le poids central de lobbies comme l'ADMD et de la Franc-maconnerie, laissent un goût d'inacheve. La procedure, centree sur un seul medecin, et l'absence de garanties plus robustes pour les personnes vulnerables alimentent les doutes sur la solidite du « modele francais » vante par l'executif.

items.description: BURKINA-KOULSE-GOUVERNANCE -PASSATION-CHARGES-GOUVERNEURE Koulsé: la gouverneure par intérim inscrit ses missions dans la dynamique de la RPP Kaya, 18 août 2026 (AIB) – La nouvelle gouverneure de la région des Koulsé et présidente de la Délégation spéciale régionale du Centre-Nord par intérim, Adenyo/Serme Bernadette, a indiqué mardi inscrire ses missions dans la dynamique de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP), appelant les forces vives de la région à « se départir de l’indifférence, de la complaisance et de l’attentisme pour faire prévaloir le sens du devoir, le patriotisme, le travail, la discipline et la responsabilité ». « Notre action administrative doit être à l’image de cette exigence qui veut une administration au service des masses laborieuses et résolument engagée dans la transformation de notre pays », a-t-elle déclaré lors de la cérémonie officielle de passation des charges, soulignant que « le contexte national commande de chacun de nous davantage de patriotisme, de courage, de cohésion, de disponibilité, de rigueur, de probité et de sens élevé du service public ». La camarade Adenyo/Sermé a appelé l’administration publique, le secteur privé, les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), les Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP), les légitimités coutumières et religieuses, les partenaires au développement et les populations à conjuguer leurs efforts face aux défis sécuritaires, sociaux et économiques. « Nous devons travailler ensemble pour bâtir une région des Koulsé résiliente et engagée dans un développement endogène », a-t-elle souligné, invitant chaque acteur à assumer pleinement ses responsabilités. La gouverneure, présidente de la délégation spéciale régionale a rassuré le personnel du gouvernorat et du Conseil régional de sa disponibilité, prônant un environnement professionnel fondé sur la confiance, le dialogue, la responsabilité, la redevabilité et le respect des textes. Pour sa part, le gouverneur sortant, le Colonel-Major Blaise Ouédraogo, a assuré sa successeure de sa disponibilité à l’accompagner dans sa mission. « La passation de charge n’est pas une rupture », a-t-il affirmé, insistant sur la continuité de l’Etat. Le personnel des deux institutions régionales, par la voix de leurs représentants, ont marqué leur engagement a accompagner la nouvelle autorité régionale et salué le bilan du colonel-major. Le secrétaire général du Conseil régional, Noufoun Ouattara, a indiqué retenir notamment du désormais député à l’ALP « sa rigueur et son sens élevé du service public, qui ont tiré chacun de nous vers le haut », ainsi que « sa vision stratégique, toujours orientée vers l’intérêt général et le développement de la région ». Il a également relevé sa volonté d’instaurer une gouvernance fondée sur « la transparence, la responsabilité, la redevabilité et le respect des procédures ». Agence d’information du Burkina AIO/bak

items.title: GoldBod ‘losses’: I’m ready to face Parliament – Sammy Gyamfi
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, has challenged Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin to use Parliament’s oversight mechanisms to invite him to answer allegations that GoldBod was responsible for massive losses incurred under the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP). Mr Gyamfi said he was ready to appear before Parliament at any time to provide evidence and defend GoldBod against the allegations. Speaking at the government’s Accountability Series on Wednesday, August 19, he said the Minority Leader should stop discussing the matter primarily at press conferences and instead trigger a parliamentary inquiry. “There has been a call for a parliamentary probe, and I’ve already stated on public record that I’m waiting with bated breath for Afenyo-Markin’s invitation,” he said. Mr Gyamfi argued that the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) already had the authority to invite him to explain GoldBod’s operations and address the allegations. “I don’t know why he’s delaying and holding press conferences when, as Minority Leader, he can get the Public Accounts Committee to summon me tomorrow or today, and I will appear,” he added. He said there was no need for a special parliamentary motion or an order from the Speaker before the committee could begin examining the matter. “I have, in all humility, reached out to the new Majority Leader in Parliament, Honourable James Agalga, and I pleaded with him that even if Afenyo-Markin delays in extending this invitation, he should extend the invitation to me, and I’m ready to come tomorrow,” he said. According to Mr Gyamfi, a parliamentary inquiry would provide an opportunity for the Minority and GoldBod to present evidence and establish where responsibility for the reported losses lies. “You don’t need any special motion; you don’t need any special order by the Speaker. Just get the Public Accounts Committee to invite us and come and sit down there and demonstrate to the whole nation where the Gold Board made losses or how the Gold Board is to blame for losses made by another institution,” he said. Gyamfi challenges claims against GoldBod Mr Gyamfi maintained that claims linking GoldBod to the reported losses under the DGPP were inaccurate and misleading. He reiterated his readiness to account for GoldBod’s operations and defend the institution against allegations that it was responsible for the financial losses. His comments follow repeated demands by Mr Afenyo-Markin for GoldBod to account for what he describes as a GH¢22 billion loss involving the state’s gold trading operations. The Minority Leader has argued that GoldBod must explain its role in transactions conducted under the DGPP and account for the financial implications of those operations. PAC chair calls for investigation Meanwhile, the Chairperson of Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee, Abena Osei-Asare, has said reports suggesting that GoldBod recorded losses amounting to US$1.7 billion, allegedly cited by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), warrant thorough investigation. She said the inquiry should establish how the reported losses occurred and whether public funds were adequately protected. Mr Gyamfi, however, has challenged Mr Afenyo-Markin to produce evidence from the IMF report that directly implicates GoldBod in losses incurred by the Bank of Ghana under the DGPP. The GoldBod CEO insists that a parliamentary inquiry would provide the appropriate platform to settle the dispute with evidence rather than competing claims in the media.

items.title: Nayala/Excellente scolaire à Kougny: les meilleurs élèves reçoivent des vélos et des kits scolaires
items.description: BURKINA-NAYALA-EDUCATION-EXCELLENCE SCOLAIRE Nayala/Excellente scolaire à Kougny: les meilleurs élèves reçoivent des vélos et des kits scolaires Kougny, 15 août 2026 (AIB) – Le Mouvement pour le Développement de Goin (MDG) dans la commune de Kougny a célébré, samedi 15 août 2026, la 5e édition de la Journée de l’excellence scolaire à l’école primaire publique de Goin, au cours de laquelle les meilleurs élèves ont été récompensés avec des vélos et des kits scolaires. Placée sous le thème « Main dans la main pour un village plus prospère : encourager le mérite, bâtir l’avenir », la cérémonie a été présidée par le président de la délégation spéciale de Kougny, Idrissa Barro. Le Camarade Barro a félicité les lauréats et les a invités à maintenir leurs efforts, rappelant que « l’excellence n’est pas seulement une bonne note ou un classement ». Il a également appelé les parents et les fils de Goin à poursuivre leur mobilisation en faveur de l’école et du CEG. Le président du MDG, Aboubacar Toé, a souligné que l’initiative vise à promouvoir l’excellence scolaire malgré le contexte sécuritaire. Il a rendu hommage aux FDS et aux VDP pour leur contribution à la réinstallation de Goin, ainsi qu’aux enseignants et aux élèves pour leur résilience. Le représentant du DPESFPT, Toné Désiré, a salué la réouverture du CEG grâce à la mobilisation des fils de Goin et félicité les différents acteurs pour leur engagement. Les trois premiers au CEP de la CEB de Kougny sont issus de l’école de Goin. La cérémonie a également été marquée par les bénédictions du chef coutumier de Goin et un slam en langue san de l’Inspecteur Sow Siaka, chef de la circonscription d’éducation de base de Kougny, sur l’alcoolisme. items.title: ‎GJA to lead nationwide media tour of galamsey-affected communities
items.description: President of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA), Albert Dwumfuor, has announced that the association will undertake a nationwide tour to assess communities and sites affected by illegal mining. ‎The exercise would involve veteran and experienced journalists who would independently examine the impact of illegal mining and engage affected communities and other key stakeholders. ‎“We will take the conversation to the ground. I will lead a team of veteran and experienced journalists on a nationwide tour of communities and sites affected by illegal mining. We will go into the field to see the situation ourselves,” he said at a national mining dialogue in Accra. ‎Mr Dwumfuor said the team would visit affected communities and mining sites and engage residents, miners, farmers, traditional leaders, regulators and other relevant stakeholders to deepen public understanding of the crisis. ‎“We will examine the conditions of previous attacks. We will speak to the affected communities. We will engage miners, farmers, traditional leaders, regulators, and other relevant stakeholders,” he said. ‎Mr Dwumfuor said the initiative would enable journalists to assess conditions on the ground rather than rely solely on reports and claims about illegal mining. ‎He said the exercise would be conducted independently of the Government, with the GJA working with development partners, experts and other relevant stakeholders considered necessary to ensure a comprehensive assessment. ‎The GJA President said the initiative formed part of the media’s responsibility to provide accurate, balanced and evidence-based reporting on the country’s mining sector. ‎He said journalists had a responsibility to investigate illegal mining networks and give affected communities a voice, while reporting fairly on interventions and mining companies that were meeting their obligations. ‎Mr Dwumfuor stressed the importance of specialised knowledge in mining journalism, saying journalists could not effectively report on an industry they did not understand. ‎He said the GJA would continue to promote specialised training for journalists covering mining, environmental issues, finance and regulation, alongside stronger fact-checking, investigative reporting and responsible use of data. ‎Mr Dwumfuor said the media must remain independent while scrutinising government policies, mining companies and regulators. ‎He said the nationwide tour would contribute to a more informed national conversation on illegal mining and the responsible exploitation of Ghana’s mineral resources.

items.title: Ghana enters Phase 2 of IAEA nuclear power programme – Lands Minister
items.description: Ghana has formally entered Phase Two of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) Milestone Approach for developing nuclear power infrastructure, marking a significant step in the country’s long-standing ambition to introduce nuclear energy into its power generation mix. Minister for Lands and Natural Resources Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah made the announcement when he delivered a speech at the US-Africa Nuclear Summit. He said Ghana had moved beyond the stage of merely aspiring to develop nuclear power, with several critical components of the programme now at an advanced stage. “Ghana has formally entered Phase Two of the International Atomic Energies Agency’s milestone approach for developing nuclear power infrastructure, detailed sites studies, institutional strengthening, stakeholder engagement, and engagement with technology vendors are all far advanced.” According to Mr Buah, the development demonstrates the progress Ghana has made in preparing the institutional and regulatory foundations required to establish a nuclear power programme. Speaking on behalf of the President, he said the country’s nuclear ambition, although interrupted over the years, had remained alive and was reactivated in 2012 under the then President John Mahama. “That ambition or that vision was interrupted, but did not die.” Mr Buah said President Mahama, during his first term in office, directed the reactivation of Ghana’s nuclear power programme, a process that was subsequently supported by constitutional and legislative reforms. The process culminated in the passage of the Nuclear Regulatory Authority Act, 2015 (Act 895), which established the regulatory framework for Ghana’s nuclear sector. He noted that successive governments had contributed to advancing the national nuclear agenda, bringing Ghana to its current stage. “And today Ghana has moved beyond aspiration. We are prepared, and so when we state that Ghana is ready, I’m here to emphasize we are truly ready. We are ready.” While highlighting Ghana’s progress, the Lands Minister said the country’s nuclear ambitions must not focus solely on the construction of nuclear facilities. He said the success of the programme would depend significantly on the availability of qualified Ghanaian and African professionals capable of designing, operating, regulating and sustaining the infrastructure. “The nuclear program is not simply a reactor; it is the people.” He said the IAEA recognises human resource development as one of the 19 infrastructure issues essential to establishing a successful nuclear power programme. Mr Buah therefore called for simultaneous investment in physical infrastructure and human capacity. “We therefore cannot build the physical infrastructure today and hope to find the people tomorrow. We must build both now.” He said Africa’s youthful population provides an opportunity to develop a strong pool of scientists, engineers, technicians, regulators, researchers and entrepreneurs who can drive the continent’s nuclear future. He called for greater investment in science, technology, engineering and mathematics education, as well as stronger universities, research institutions and postgraduate programmes.

items.title: Angélique Kidjo, première chanteuse africaine à obtenir son étoile sur l’Allée des célébrités d’Hollywood
items.description: L'artiste franco-béninoise, Angélique Kidjo, détentrice de cinq Grammys, est la première chanteuse africaine à obtenir son étoile sur l’Allée des célébrités «Walk of Fame», le mardi 18 août 2026, à Los Angeles. Angélique Kidjo est devenue la première chanteuse africaine à disposer d’une étoile incrustée sur le prestigieux « Walk of Fame (Allée des célébrités) », lors d'une cérémonie qui s’est déroulée, le mardi 18 août 2026, à Los Angeles, aux Etats-Unis d’Amérique. Le trottoir du Hollywood Boulevard est pavé de sa 2 854e étoile, celle de Angélique Kidjo qui compte plus de quatre décennies de carrière internationale marquée par de nombreux succès. Cinq fois lauréate d’un Grammy Award et autrice de 18 albums, Angélique Kidjo s’est imposée comme l’une des grandes voix africaines sur les scènes internationales. Aujourd’hui âgée de 66 ans, l’artiste a souligné au cours de la cérémonie la contribution méconnue du continent africain à la musique planétaire. «Nous, les Africains, ne savons pas ce que nous avons donné au monde, et ce que nous continuons de lui donner pour que la musique existe. […] Sans nous, aucune musique n’est possible sur cette planète», a-t-elle dit. Le gouvernement du Bénin s’est réjoui de cette «consécration» de celle qui «porte haut l’image du (pays) sur la scène internationale». Dans un communiqué, la productrice du Walk of Fame, Ana Martinez, a souligné que «le talent artistique exceptionnel et l’influence mondiale d’Angélique Kidjo ont inspiré des publics de toutes les générations et de tous les continents», et salué en elle la première artiste africaine à recevoir une étoile depuis la création de cette distinction, en 1960. Repérée au début des années 80 par Chris Blackwell, producteur de Bob Marley, Angélique Kidjo a toujours brassé les influences, revisitant le Boléro de Ravel ou la Pop des Talking Heads. Par Wakat Séra L’article Angélique Kidjo, première chanteuse africaine à obtenir son étoile sur l’Allée des célébrités d'Hollywood est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Nayala: l’Assomption célébrée à Toma sous le signe de la foi et de la fraternité
items.description: BURKINA-NAYALA-ASSOMPTION-CELEBRATION Nayala: l’Assomption célébrée à Toma sous le signe de la foi et de la fraternité Toma, 15 août 2026 (AIB) – Les fidèles catholiques de la paroisse Sacré-Cœur de Toma ont célébré, samedi 15 août 2026, la solennité de l’Assomption de la Vierge Marie, en présence des premières autorités de la province. La célébration a débuté à la grotte mariale par une procession jusqu’à l’église Sacré-Cœur, où la messe a été concélébrée par le curé, l’abbé Jean Gourou, et l’abbé Jean-Paul Soro. Dans son homélie, l’abbé Jean Gourou a présenté Marie comme un modèle pour l’humanité, invitant les fidèles à cultiver l’action de grâce, à reconnaître le bien et à discerner les signes qui conduisent vers Dieu. Les prières universelles ont porté sur le pape, les malades, la paix au Burkina Faso, le retour des personnes déplacées et la conversion des auteurs de violences. Le haut-commissaire du Nayala, Honoré Frédéric Paré, a salué l’engagement des responsables religieux et réaffirmé la disponibilité de l’administration provinciale à accompagner la paroisse. Il a invité les fidèles à accueillir la transition dans « la foi, la sérénité et la fraternité », avant de confier la paroisse, le Nayala et le Burkina Faso à l’intercession de la Vierge Marie. items.title: 'A good start': PPP, opposition agree to maintain contact, cooperate on legislative matters in parliament
items.description: ISLAMABAD: In a significant move, PPP, a major ruling coalition partner, and the opposition PTI on Wednesday agreed to maintain contact and cooperate on legislative matters in the parliament. The agreement was reached when PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari met Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Leader of the Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas at the Parliament House in the NA opposition leader’s chamber, PPP said in a post on X. PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP) Secretary General Asad Qaiser, Vice Chairman Mustafa Nawaz Khokhar and PTI’s Aamir Dogar were also present at the meeting. PPP leaders Raja Pervez Ashraf, Sherry Rehman, Naveed Qamar and Nadeem Afzal Chan accompanied Bilawal. The meeting discussed parliamentary affairs and the country’s political situation. Bilawal asked the opposition leaders to join parliamentary committees and play an active role, according to the statement. The opposition leaders said they would decide after consulting the PTI chairman, it added. The PPP and opposition leaders agreed to increase contact regarding legislation in parliament. Bilawal urged the opposition leaders to play their role in parliament in connection with electoral reforms to ensure transparency in elections. Referring to the transfer of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan to the hospital and his treatment following the Supreme Court’s decision , Bilawal welcomed the development, saying that it was a democratic tradition. Speaking to the media later in the day, Bilawal termed the meeting a “good start” and said that his party wanted the House to be functional and that the parliamentarians should play their role as mandated by the public. “If we want our parliament to be functional and its institutions or dignitaries to work, then the opposition should review their decision of boycotting the parliamentary process,” he said. He said that he discussed reviewing the opposition’s decision to boycott the parliamentary process in the meeting. “Whether you are sitting on opposition benches or treasury benches, everyone complains about the electoral process; [so] then it is our responsibility to make reforms in our electoral process,” the PPP chairman said. For this single-point agenda, Bilawal said that the opposition should play its role so that a plan may be formulated for reforms in the electoral process through mutual consensus. “When a party wins elections, it celebrates, and when a party loses elections, it complains; we don’t want this.” The PPP chairman further stated that a “communication gap” between his party and the opposition had been lessened after today’s meeting and the two sides had initiated discussions on several issues, particularly the “low-hanging fruits” such as electoral reforms. On being asked about the possibility of the 28th Constitutional Amendment, the PPP chairman said there had been no discussions between the PPP and PML-N on the matter. Regarding the creation of new provinces, the PPP chairman said that his party would stand by the public’s decision. “The PPP will stand with the public’s opinion, and whatever decision is taken with mutual understanding, the party will support it. We will never accept anything by force,” he stated. On Tuesday, it emerged that the PPP had reached out to the opposition alliance to seek its cooperation and was expected to call on Achakzai today. Sources told Dawn that the agenda for the cooperation is to work together to strengthen the parliament and parliament’s committees. Talking to Dawn on Tuesday, a senior PTI leader had said that it seemed the PPP was trying to “raise its value” through such moves. However, “we will support any party that talks about free and fair elections and stopping rigging through Form 47s”, the leader said. Insiders suggest that while the PPP cannot afford to formally exit the coalition government at the Centre, it could give the government a tough time to show its displeasure over the outcome of the AJK elections. Over the past couple of weeks, several PPP leaders — including the party chief — had accused the ruling party of ‘rigging’ and manipulating election results.

items.title: Burkina : Le Ministère de la jeunesse lance un appel à candidatures pour le bureau exécutif du futur « Conseil National Consultatif de la Jeunesse »
items.description: Le Ministère des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l'Emploi a officiellement ouvert, ce 19 août 2026, un appel à candidatures pour la nomination des membres du Bureau Exécutif National (BEN) et des Commissions Spécialisées du futur « Conseil National Consultatif de la Jeunesse du Burkina Faso » (CNCJ-BF). Le Ministère de la jeunesse lance un appel à candidatures pour le bureau exécutif du futur « Conseil National Consultatif de la Jeunesse du Burkina Faso ». Cette instance, qui se veut le mécanisme transitoire de la faîtière des organisations de jeunesse, a pour mission de structurer et de représenter le mouvement associatif jeune à l'échelle nationale. Le Bureau Exécutif National sera composé de sept membres : un président, deux vice-présidents (dont au moins une jeune fille), trois rapporteurs généraux (dont au moins une jeune fille), ainsi qu'un secrétaire chargé du genre et de la promotion des jeunes, un secrétaire chargé de la communication et du partenariat, un trésorier général et un trésorier adjoint. Parallèlement, six commissions thématiques sont créées pour animer les travaux du Conseil : affaires sociales, affaires économiques, affaires institutionnelles et juridiques, environnement et ressources naturelles, culture et sport, ainsi que sécurité, paix et migration. Chaque commission sera dirigée par un bureau de séance composé d'un président et de deux rapporteurs, dont au moins une jeune fille, et ne pourra compter plus de cinq membres, tous nommés par le ministre. Peuvent postuler les jeunes Burkinabè âgés de 15 à 34 ans au 30 septembre 2026, jouissant d'une bonne moralité, sachant lire et écrire en français, et mandatés par une association de jeunes ou de jeunesse reconnue par le ministère en charge des libertés publiques. Chaque organisation ne peut soumettre qu'une seule candidature et délivrer qu'un seul mandat. Les dossiers, à retirer dans les Directions Provinciales en charge de la Jeunesse, doivent comporter une fiche de candidature signée, une photocopie du récépissé de l'association, une copie de la CNIB ou du passeport en cours de validité, et le cas échéant, un mandat de l'association si le candidat n'en est pas le premier responsable. Ils sont recevables du 19 au 21 août 2026, de 08h à 15h, dans toutes les Directions Provinciales des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l'Emploi. Le Ministère de la jeunesse précise qu'une association ne peut avoir plus d'un représentant au sein du CNCJ-BF, et invite les intéressés à contacter les directions provinciales et régionales pour toute information complémentaire.
